title: Conjecture 1.4
statement_text: For every fixed positive $p \leq 1$, Erdős-Rényi random graph $G(n, 1-p)$ a.a.s. has correspondence chromatic number $\Theta(n/\log n)$.
context_text: $G(n,1-p)$ is the Erdős–Rényi random graph in which each pair of vertices is an edge independently with probability $1-p$ (so for $p<1$ it is dense; for $p=1$ it is edgeless and the statement is degenerate). Correspondence coloring (DP-coloring, Dvořák and Postle) generalizes list coloring: a correspondence assignment $(L,M)$ gives each vertex $v$ a list $L(v)$ and each edge $uv$ a (not necessarily perfect) matching $M_{uv}$ between $\{u\}\times L(u)$ and $\{v\}\times L(v)$; an $(L,M)$-coloring picks $\varphi(v)\in L(v)$ for every $v$ such that $(u,\varphi(u))$ and $(v,\varphi(v))$ are not matched in $M_{uv}$ for any edge $uv$; the correspondence chromatic number is the least $\ell$ such that $G$ is $(L,M)$-colorable for every assignment with all $|L(v)|\ge\ell$. Lower bound: $G(n,1-p)$ a.a.s. has independence number $O(\log n)$, so already $\chi=\Omega(n/\log n)$, and Bernshteyn's bound $\Omega(d/\log d)$ for graphs of average degree $d$ gives the same. The authors prove the upper bound $O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$ a.a.s., which matches the Hadwiger number $\Theta(n/\sqrt{\log n})$ of $G(n,p)$ and thus supports Linear Hadwiger's conjecture for correspondence coloring. Both extreme kinds of assignment need only $O(n/\log n)$ colors: list assignments (the list chromatic number of $G(n,1-p)$ is $O(n/\log n)$ a.a.s.) and uniformly random assignments with perfect matchings, for which they show that even $K_n$ is a.a.s. colorable with $\Theta(n/\log n)$ colors. The authors hope the conjecture is false, as this would separate list and correspondence chromatic numbers in a new way.
